newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Placer, CVG gold rights secure - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Placer, CVG gold rights secure - Minister.

text.p: Concession rights by Placer Dome Inc, and its joint venture partner Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana's (CVG), over the Las Cristinas project gold project are secure, Venezuelan vice-minister for Energy and Mines Evanan Romero said on Tuesday.
"We have absolutely no doubts as to the legal clarity (of the concessions)," Evanan Romero told reporters at an oil and mining seminar.

Rival mining group Crystallex International Corp has said it acquired rights to two blocks of the property by buying a Venezuelan company "whose ownership rights have been confirmed by final and binding decisions" of Venezuela's Supreme Court.
But Placer said late Monday the Supreme Court decisions on which Crystallex based its claims "are wholly irrelevant to the right of tenure of CVG. Hence the rights ... are secure and valid in law."
In 1991, the Ministry granted the rights to Las Cristinas to the CVG, which struck a $576 million joint venture with Placer in 1992. Placer holds 70 percent and the CVG the rest.
